question: GQ-001
action: sixth and final re-derivation — the last self-referential claim

what_i_could_not_count.attempted: Classifying every defect in 134 worklogs as gate-caught vs execution-caught, by keyword.
what_i_could_not_count.why_i_discarded_it: Sampling the matches showed the keywords do not mean what the count implies. Lines like "CAUGHT: ['npm run mailbox:flush']" are me DEMONSTRATING a gate fires on a deliberate fixture, not a gate catching a real defect. A keyword count over prose is the same shallow-proxy mistake as ranking databases by size or classifying launchd jobs by ProgramArguments[0].
what_i_could_not_count.decision: Not publishing a ratio I cannot defend. The original 3-vs-6 was hand-counted over one session; there is no honest mechanical successor to it.

what_is_countable.gate_selftest_cases_note: was 12; re-derived 2026-08-04 after two cases were added — one proving the source-coverage gate fires, one proving a prose mention does not count as a script reference. The audit caught this because the number was DECLARED; an undeclared count would have aged silently.

the_zero_is_a_finding: verify has never blocked a push — not because it never fails, but because every push in this repo runs it first and stops voluntarily. The gate is a pre-commit habit, not an enforcement boundary. Nothing prevents a push that skips it.
the_selftest_finding: When the gate self-test was first run it found the refresh evaluator swallowing all git errors and returning an empty commit list — reporting ten entries fresh from zero information. That is one defect found BY A GATE-CHECKER rather than by a gate, which is a third category the original claim did not have.
verdict: The claim's DIRECTION survives — gates and execution catch different classes, and this session produced repeated examples of defects only execution could find. Its NUMBERS are stale and I cannot honestly refresh the ratio. Position rewritten to assert the distinction and drop the un-reproducible count.
